reasons: **Heat safety comes first, with very little room to spare.** Even the crew members who heat up the most should stay just under the body-temperature safety limit, but at the tightest point the margin is less than a tenth of a degree. Watch closely for signs of heat stress, and enforce breaks, shade, and water. Don't add extra work.

**We'll get most of the important work done, but not all of it.** This plan finishes about 84% of the priority work. It's also built around two hard rules: no outdoor work from 1:30 to 3:00 because of lightning, and Wei, who is new and not yet used to the heat, gets no very heavy jobs when it's hot.

**We picked the coolest option.** A plan that pushes harder would finish a bit more work (87%) but run the crew hotter, right up against the limit. Hard safety rules:
- Every worker's 90th percentile core temperature must stay below 38.0 °C all shift. Harder work, sun and high WBGT heat people up; 30-min shade rests cool them down.
- Breaks: at most 3 work slots in a row, then a 'rest' slot; at most 2 in a row if any of those slots has WBGT >= 30.0 °C.
- No outdoor tasks during hazards that stop outdoor work. After lightning, outdoor work stays stopped for 30 more minutes.
- Workers who are not acclimatized never do very_heavy tasks when WBGT >= 28.0 °C.
Validity: one entry per slot per worker; off-site workers rest; skills and allowed slots must match.
